# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/__init__.py](src/__init__.py)
- [src/model/surpass.py](src/model/surpass.py)
- [src/train.py](src/train.py)

</details>



SurPass is a deep learning framework designed for protein-protein interaction (PPI) and inter-chain contact prediction [src/train.py:1-35](). It leverages protein language model (pLM) embeddings combined with sequence features to model residue and pair representations through an iterative transformer and geometric update architecture [src/model/surpass.py:28-192]().

The core model architecture, `ResOnly` [src/model/surpass.py:28](), processes residue tokens and pair representations through stacked residue transformers [src/model/surpass.py:75](), outer product mean modules [src/model/surpass.py:90](), and triangle update layers [src/model/surpass.py:98-110](). It produces outputs structured in `SurpassOutput` [src/model/surpass.py:20-26](), which include pair distogram logits, residue-level binding scores, and whole-protein interaction logits [src/model/surpass.py:187-191]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Protein Sequence & pLM Embeddings"] --> B["ResidueEmbedder src/model/components/embedder.py"]
    B --> C["ResOnly Model src/model/surpass.py"]
    C --> D["ResidueTransformer src/model/components/transformer.py"]
    C --> E["EfficientOuterProductMean src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py"]
    C --> F["Triangle Updates src/model/components/triangle_update.py"]
    C --> G["SurpassOutput src/model/surpass.py"]
    G --> H["Pair Logits / Distograms src/train.py"]
    G --> I["Residue Bind Scores src/train.py"]
    G --> J["Protein Logit src/train.py"]
```

Sources: `src/model/surpass.py:20-192]`, `src/train.py:1-35`

## 1.1 Getting Started & Environment

The repository provides automated installation procedures and structured entry points for running training pipelines, inference jobs, and diagnostic previews. The environment setup relies on configuration files that manage dependencies across compute hardware, including distributed training support.

For details on setting up the environment, repository layout, and launching entry points, see [Getting Started & Environment](#1.1).

Sources: `src/train.py:1-45`

## 1.2 Configuration System (Hydra)

SurPass utilizes Hydra to manage configurations for training and inference workflows. Configuration schemas are split into modular blocks covering data loaders, network architecture parameters, loss weighting schemes, optimizers, and experiment tracking via Weights & Biases (`wandb`).

For details on config schemas and parameter mapping, see [Configuration System (Hydra)](#1.2).

Sources: `src/train.py:6-10`, `src/model/surpass.py:28-46`

# Page: Getting Started & Environment

# Getting Started & Environment

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

## Purpose and Scope
This page outlines the technical setup, environment configuration, repository organization, and execution entrypoints for the SurPass codebase. SurPass relies on PyTorch and Hydra for flexible configuration and distributed training. Here we detail how to set up the runtime environment using `env.yaml` and `setup.py`, understand the directory layout, and launch core execution pipelines.

Sources: [src/__init__.py:1-1](), [env.yaml:1-25](), [setup.py:1-14]()

---

## Environment Installation
SurPass manages its dependencies via Conda and pip. The environment specification is provided in `env.yaml`, which sets up Python 3.11 alongside deep learning libraries (`torch==2.6.0`, `torch-geometric`) and data processing utilities (`biopython`, `biopandas`, `hydra-core`, `wandb`) [env.yaml:1-25]().

### Installation Steps
1. Create and activate the Conda environment named `idpfold2` using the specification file [env.yaml:1-1]():
   ```bash
   conda env create -f env.yaml
   conda activate idpfold2
   ```
2. Install the local package in editable mode using `setup.py`:
   ```bash
   pip install -e .
   ```

### Dependency Stack Summary
| Category | Packages / Tools | Source Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Runtime** | `python=3.11`, `torch==2.6.0`, `torch-geometric`, `numpy==1.26.0` | [env.yaml:5-16]() |
| **Configuration & Logging** | `hydra-core==1.3.1`, `wandb`, `loguru==0.7.2`, `rootutils` | [env.yaml:11-25]() |
| **Protein Processing** | `biopython`, `biopandas==0.5.1`, `biotite`, `cpdb-protein` | [env.yaml:19-22]() |
| **Utilities** | `einops==0.6`, `dm-tree==0.1.8`, `pandas==1.5.3`, `scikit-learn>=1.3` | [env.yaml:9-24]() |

Sources: [env.yaml:1-25](), [setup.py:1-14]()

---

## Repository Layout & Build Configuration
The repository is structured around a modular Python package rooted in `src/`, with configuration files and helper scripts organized cleanly. Build metadata is defined in `setup.py` [setup.py:4-14](), which automatically discovers internal packages.

```
SurPass/
├── env.yaml            # Conda environment specification
├── setup.py            # Package installation script
├── .gitignore          # Git exclusion patterns
├── src/                # Core source code package
│   ├── __init__.py     # Package marker
│   ├── common/         # Shared constants and utilities
│   ├── data/           # Dataset pipelines, cropping, and collation
│   ├── models/         # ResOnly neural network architecture
│   └── utils/          # DDP, tensor, and windowing utilities
└── configs/            # Hydra configuration yaml files
```

### Git Ignores
Transient directories such as local logs, generated outputs, python cache files, and test artifacts are excluded from version control via `.gitignore` [-.gitignore:1-8]().

Sources: [.gitignore:1-8](), [setup.py:1-14](), [src/__init__.py:1-1]()

---

## Execution Entrypoints & Workflows
SurPass operates through distinct entrypoints managed by Hydra configuration blocks. The training system, inference pipeline, and visualization tools are invoked from command-line interfaces driven by configuration YAML files.

### 1. Training Entrypoint
Training is driven by distributed data parallel (DDP) execution models, orchestrating dataset multi-source balancing, loss calculation, and optimization.

### 2. Inference Pipeline
Inference execution evaluates trained checkpoints against FASTA and embedding inputs, utilizing long-sequence windowing algorithms for complex protein structures.

### 3. Preview Utilities
Debugging and preview scripts allow direct spatial visualization of distance maps and NaN monitoring during development.

```mermaid

    C -->|BuildsPackage| D["src"]
    
    subgraph "Execution Surfaces"
        D --> E["TrainingEntryPoint"]
        D --> F["InferencePipeline"]
        D --> G["PreviewUtility"]
    end

    E -->|ConfiguresVia| H["configs/train.yaml"]
    F -->|ConfiguresVia| I["configs/inference.yaml"]
    G -->|MonitorsTensors| J["src/preview.py"]
```

# Page: Configuration System (Hydra)

# Configuration System (Hydra)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/inference.yaml](configs/inference.yaml)
- [configs/train.yaml](configs/train.yaml)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the configuration schema and management system used in SurPass, driven by Facebook Hydra. It covers the structural schemas of `configs/train.yaml` and `configs/inference.yaml`, detailing how configuration blocks (`data`, `model`, `loss`, `optimizer`, `wandb`, `hydra`, and `performance`) map directly to python code structures, dataset loaders, neural network modules, and training/inference execution routines.

Sources: `configs/train.yaml:1-127` [configs/train.yaml:1-126](), `configs/inference.yaml:1-53` [configs/inference.yaml:1-52]()

---

## Configuration Architecture and YAML Schemas

SurPass uses Hydra to manage hyper-parameters, data paths, model dimensions, and optimization details. Configuration files are split into training (`configs/train.yaml`) and inference (`configs/inference.yaml`) profiles. 

### Global Runtime Settings
* `task_prefix`: A string prefix used for logging and run identification (`configs/train.yaml:1-1` [], `configs/inference.yaml:1-1` []).
* `seed`: Random seed for reproducibility across runs (`configs/train.yaml:3-3` [], `configs/inference.yaml:3-3` []).
* `deterministic`: Boolean flag to enforce deterministic algorithms in PyTorch (`configs/train.yaml:4-4` [], `configs/inference.yaml:4-4` []).
* `ckpt_dir`: Path to checkpoint directories for resuming training or loading weights for inference (`configs/train.yaml:7-7` [], `configs/inference.yaml:5-5` []).

```mermaid
graph TD
    YAML["configs/train.yaml"] --> Global["Global Settings (seed, deterministic, task_prefix)"]
    YAML --> DataBlock["data: root_dir, datasets, batch_size, crop_size"]
    YAML --> ModelBlock["model: n_layers, dim_token, dim_pair, n_heads"]
    YAML --> LossBlock["loss: intra, inter, focal, mae, tversky"]
    YAML --> OptBlock["optimizer: lr, weight_decay, lr_scheduler"]
    YAML --> WandbBlock["wandb: project, entity, mode"]
    YAML --> HydraBlock["hydra: run.dir, output_subdir"]
```
*Sources: `configs/train.yaml:1-123` [configs/train.yaml:1-123]()*

---

## Data Block Schema

The `data` block configures dataset paths, multiprocessing parameters, negative sampling ratios, distance binning, and spatial cropping.

### Training Data Configuration (`configs/train.yaml`)
* `root_dir`: Base directory containing all training datasets (`configs/train.yaml:16-16` []).
* `epoch_size`: Number of samples per training epoch (`configs/train.yaml:17-17` []).
* `datasets`: A multi-source dataset list specifying `pdb_ppi`, `afdb_pos`, and `afdb_neg` subdirectories, cluster TSV files, assembly flags, and sampling weights (`configs/train.yaml:18-35` []).
* `batch_size` & `num_workers`: DataLoader batch configuration (`configs/train.yaml:36-37` []).
* `negative_ratio`: Ratio of negative to positive pairs during negative assembly (`configs/train.yaml:40-40` []).
* `distance_bin_start`, `distance_bin_end`, `distance_bin_count`: Parameters defining the distogram discretization range (2.0Å to 22.0Å over 64 bins) (`configs/train.yaml:41-43` []).
* `crop_size` & `crop_contiguous_prob`: Spatial and contiguous cropping parameters for residue pair matrices (`configs/train.yaml:45-46` []).

### Inference Data Configuration (`configs/inference.yaml`)
* `test_set_tsv` & `fasta_path`: Paths to evaluation tabular data and input FASTA sequences (`configs/inference.yaml:9-10` []).
* `embedding_dir`: Directory containing precomputed protein language model (pLM) embeddings (`configs/inference.yaml:11-11` []).
* `max_full_length`: Maximum sequence length supported in full-length inference before windowing (`configs/inference.yaml:15-15` []).
* `ppi_score_threshold`: Threshold used to call predicted inter-chain contacts or interfaces (`configs/inference.yaml:20-20` []).

```mermaid
graph TD
    DataSchema["data block in YAML"] -->|root_dir & subdir| Dataset["PepoTrainDataset / InferencePairDataset"]
    DataSchema -->|crop_size / crop_contiguous_prob| Cropping["src/data/cropping.py"]
    DataSchema -->|distance_bin_*| Distogram["Distance Binning & Labels"]
    DataSchema -->|batch_size / num_workers| DataLoader["PyTorch DataLoader"]
```
*Sources: `configs/train.yaml:15-47` [configs/train.yaml:15-47](), `configs/inference.yaml:7-21` [configs/inference.yaml:7-21]()*

---

## Model Block Schema

The `model` block configures the architecture dimensions, network depth, and attention mechanisms of the `ResOnly` network.

* `n_layers`: Number of stacked transformer layers (`configs/train.yaml:49-49` [], `configs/inference.yaml:26-26` []).
* `dim_token`: Dimensionality of the residue/token stream (`configs/train.yaml:50-50` [], `configs/inference.yaml:27-27` []).
* `dim_pair`: Dimensionality of the pair representation stream (`configs/train.yaml:51-51` [], `configs/inference.yaml:28-28` []).
* `n_heads`: Number of attention heads in multi-head attention blocks (`configs/train.yaml:52-52` [], `configs/inference.yaml:29-29` []).
* `use_attn_pair_bias` & `use_qkln`: Flags enabling pair-wise attention biases and Query-Key Layer Normalization (`configs/train.yaml:55-56` [], `configs/inference.yaml:32-33` []).
* `plm_in_dim` & `plm_out_dim`: Input and projected dimensions for pLM embeddings (`configs/train.yaml:59-60` [], `configs/inference.yaml:36-37` []).
* `r_max`: Maximum residue separation distance considered for relative positional encodings (`configs/train.yaml:61-61` [], `configs/inference.yaml:38-38` []).
* `dim_opm_inner` & `dim_triangle_hidden`: Inner dimensions for Outer Product Mean and Triangle update modules (`configs/train.yaml:65-66` [], `configs/inference.yaml:42-43` []).
* `num_classes`: Number of discrete distance bins for output prediction heads (`configs/train.yaml:67-67` [], `configs/inference.yaml:44-44` []).

Sources: `configs/train.yaml:48-68` [configs/train.yaml:48-68](), `configs/inference.yaml:25-45` [configs/inference.yaml:25-45]()

---

## Loss, Optimizer, and Training Execution Blocks

Training-specific blocks control objective functions, optimization schedules, EMA, and experiment tracking.

### Loss Configuration (`configs/train.yaml`)
* `intra` & `inter`: Weighting factors for intra-chain versus inter-chain pairs (`configs/train.yaml:70-71` []).
* `focal`: Focal loss sub-block containing `weight`, `gamma`, and `alpha` (`configs/train.yaml:73-76` []).
* `mae` & `tversky`: Supplementary loss configurations (`configs/train.yaml:77-82` []).
* `residue_bind` & `protein`: Interface binding classification objectives (`configs/train.yaml:83-88` []).
* `consistency`: Geometric/structural consistency loss term (`configs/train.yaml:89-90` []).

### Optimizer & EMA Configuration (`configs/train.yaml`)
* `optimizer`: Configures `lr` (0.0005), `weight_decay` (1e-6), Adam parameters, `lr_scheduler` (`af3`), warmup steps, gradient accumulation steps (`grad_accum_steps: 4`), and gradient clipping (`max_grad_norm: 1.0`) (`configs/train.yaml:92-103` []).
* `ema`: Exponential Moving Average settings including `decay` (0.999) and mutable parameter keywords (`configs/train.yaml:11-13` []).
* `wandb`: Weights & Biases integration parameters (`enabled`, `project`, `entity`, `mode`, `tags`) (`configs/train.yaml:108-117` []).

```mermaid
graph TD
    LossSchema["loss block in YAML"] --> Focal["Focal Loss (gamma, alpha)"]
    LossSchema --> Tversky["Tversky Loss (alpha, beta)"]
    LossSchema --> Bind["Residue & Protein Binding Loss"]
    OptSchema["optimizer block in YAML"] --> Adam["AdamW Optimizer"]
    OptSchema --> Sched["AlphaFold3 LR Scheduler"]
    OptSchema --> Grad["Gradient Accumulation & Clipping"]
```
*Sources: `configs/train.yaml:11-14` [configs/train.yaml:11-14](), `configs/train.yaml:69-117` [configs/train.yaml:69-117]()*

---

# Page: Data Pipeline

# Data Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/__init__.py](src/data/__init__.py)
- [src/data/balancing.py](src/data/balancing.py)
- [src/data/dataset.py](src/data/dataset.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The data pipeline in SurPass is responsible for transforming raw protein structural data, protein Language Model (pLM) embeddings, and PPI cluster annotations into model-ready batches. It manages the ingestion of paired chain features, spatial or contiguous cropping for memory efficiency, distance binning for distogram prediction, negative sampling for contrastive/binary learning, dataset balancing across multiple data sources, and collation into variable-length concatenated pair tensors.

This page provides a high-level parent overview of the data pipeline sub-systems. For deep technical implementation details, refer to the individual child sections:
- [PepoTrainDataset and Feature Loading](#2.1)
- [Cropping, Labels and Collation](#2.2)
- [Multi-Source Balancing and Splits](#2.3)
- [Dataset Preparation Scripts](#2.4)

Sources: [src/data/dataset.py:26-167](), [src/data/balancing.py:1-106]()

---

## Data Pipeline Architecture Overview

The pipeline integrates multiple stages from raw dataset preparation scripts to batched training inputs. The diagram below bridges the natural language conceptual flow to the core codebase entities involved in dataset construction and batching.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub-DataIngestion["Data Ingestion & Loading"]
      Prep["Scripts & Preparation (scripts/)"] --> TSV["Cluster TSV Metadata (src/data/dataset.py)"]
      TSV --> PTD["PepoTrainDataset (src/data/dataset.py:26-40)"]
    end

    sub-PairSampling["Pair Sampling & Cropping"]
      PTD -->|Positive Pair| Pos["_positive_sample_from_row (src/data/dataset.py:108-134)"]
      PTD -->|Negative Pair| Neg["get_negative_item / get_static_negative_item (src/data/dataset.py:135-149)"]
      Pos --> Crop["crop_positive_pair / crop_negative_pair (src/data/cropping.py)"]
      Neg --> Crop
    end

    sub-LabelsAndBatching["Labels & Collation"]
      Crop --> Labels["distance_to_bins / build_negative_pair_labels (src/data/labels.py)"]
      Labels --> Collate["collate_concatenated_pairs (src/data/collate.py)"]
      Collate --> Sampler["DistributedWeightedSampler (src/data/balancing.py:131-182)"]
    end

    Collate --> Model["Model Training / Inference (src/models/)"]

    classDef default font-family:sans-serif;
```
*Figure 2.1: High-level mapping from dataset preparation and ingestion to collation and model consumption.*

Sources: [src/data/dataset.py:26-167](), [src/data/balancing.py:131-182](), [src/data/__init__.py:1-25]()

---

## 2.1 PepoTrainDataset and Feature Loading

The core dataset class `PepoTrainDataset` (`[src/data/dataset.py:26]`) indexes protein-protein interaction (PPI) clusters from a metadata TSV file (`[src/data/dataset.py:62-76]`). It coordinates positive sampling from true interacting pairs within the same cluster and negative sampling across distinct clusters (`[src/data/dataset.py:81-149]`).

Chain features (such as pLM embeddings and residue positions) are loaded from `.pt` files and preprocessed via `_process_complex` before pairing. Distance matrices and labels are dynamically fetched or calculated to prepare training items.

For full implementation details, see [PepoTrainDataset and Feature Loading](#2.1).

Sources: [src/data/dataset.py:26-149]()

---

## 2.2 Cropping, Labels and Collation

Because protein complexes vary dramatically in sequence length, the pipeline applies spatial or contiguous cropping via `src/data/cropping.py` to bound memory consumption (`[src/data/dataset.py:114-123]`). Ground-truth inter-chain and intra-chain distances are converted into discrete distance bins (`[src/data/dataset.py:127-132]`) defined in `src/data/labels.py`.

Finally, variable-sized residue pairs are batched using specialized collation routines like `collate_concatenated_pairs` (`[src/data/collate.py]`), handling padding and mask generation for PyTorch data loaders.

For full implementation details, see [Cropping, Labels and Collation](#2.2).

Sources: [src/data/dataset.py:114-133](), [src/data/collate.py:1-9]()

---

## 2.3 Multi-Source Balancing and Splits

To handle multiple data sources and prevent class imbalance between positive interactions and negative non-interacting pairs, SurPass provides dataset wrappers and samplers (`[src/data/balancing.py]`). 

`BalancedClusterDataset` (`[src/data/balancing.py:33]`) pairs positive items with a configurable `negative_ratio` (`[src/data/balancing.py:39]`). Additionally, `DistributedWeightedSampler` (`[src/data/balancing.py:131]`) facilitates distributed training (DDP) by drawing replacement samples according to source-specific dataset weights across ranks (`[src/data/balancing.py:172-181]`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub-BalancingAndSplits["Balancing & Splitting Module (src/data/balancing.py)"]
      Split["split_dataset (src/data/balancing.py:13-30)"] --> TrainSet["Train Subset"]
      Split --> TestSet["Test Subset"]
      TrainSet --> Bal["BalancedClusterDataset (src/data/balancing.py:33-64)"]
      TestSet --> BalTest["BalancedClusterDataset (Test)"]
      Bal --> Sampler["DistributedWeightedSampler (src/data/balancing.py:131-182)"]
    end

    classDef default font-family:sans-serif;
```
*Figure 2.2: Data balancing and distributed sampling structure.*

For full implementation details, see [Multi-Source Balancing and Splits](#2.3).

Sources: [src/data/balancing.py:13-182]()

---

## 2.4 Dataset Preparation Scripts

Prior to training, raw databases must be processed through preparation scripts located in `scripts/`. These pipelines handle PDB entry parsing, AlphaFold Database (AFDB) domain verification, MMSeqs2 sequence clustering and redundancy filtering, pLM embedding generation (e.g., via ESMC), and UniProt sequence fetching.

For full implementation details, see [Dataset Preparation Scripts](#2.4).

Sources: [src/data/dataset.py:41-43]()

---

# Page: PepoTrainDataset and Feature Loading

# PepoTrainDataset and Feature Loading

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/dataset.py](src/data/dataset.py)
- [src/data/preprocess.py](src/data/preprocess.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the implementation of `PepoTrainDataset` and the associated feature loading pipeline in the SurPass codebase. The dataset handles protein-protein interaction (PPI) clusters, executes positive and negative sampling strategies, loads precomputed chain feature PyTorch tensors (`.pt`), processes distance labels from pickled files, and normalizes tensors via complex processing methods.

---

## 1. PepoTrainDataset Initialization and Cluster Organization

The `PepoTrainDataset` class inherits from `torch.utils.data.Dataset` and is designed to load protein-protein interaction pairs grouped by structural similarity clusters (`ppi_cluster_id`) [src/data/dataset.py:26-40]().

During initialization, the dataset reads a metadata TSV file (`cluster_tsv_path`) containing cluster assignments and file paths [src/data/dataset.py:62-63](). It validates the presence of required columns (`chain1`, `chain2`, `ppi_cluster_id`, and optionally `label_path`) [src/data/dataset.py:63-70](). The dataset indexes unique PPI clusters to balance sampling across distinct structural families rather than individual complex instances [src/data/dataset.py:72-76]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Cluster TSV File"] --> B["pd.read_csv(cluster_tsv_path)"]
    B --> C["PepoTrainDataset.__init__"]
    C --> D["Validate Required Columns: chain1, chain2, ppi_cluster_id, label_path"]
    C --> E["Group Metadata by ppi_cluster_id -> self.cluster_to_rows"]
    C --> F["Extract Unique Clusters -> self.items"]

    style A fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style E fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Diagram 1: Initialization flow of `PepoTrainDataset` mapping TSV metadata into cluster groupings.*

Sources: `[src/data/dataset.py:26-76]()`

---

## 2. Positive Sampling and Chain Feature Loading

When indexing the dataset via `__getitem__`, it delegates to `get_positive_item(idx)` [src/data/dataset.py:81-82](). This method selects a random row from the specified PPI cluster, shuffling available structural representatives until a valid positive pair containing an inter-chain contact is found [src/data/dataset.py:94-106]().

The chain features are loaded via `_load_pair_features`, which retrieves chain features and normalizes them through `_process_complex` [src/data/dataset.py:89-92](). Pairwise distances and masks are loaded from label paths, after which `crop_positive_pair` is invoked to extract spatial or contiguous sub-crops [src/data/dataset.py:108-123](). Finally, continuous distance matrices are converted into discrete distance bins using `distance_to_bins` [src/data/dataset.py:127-132]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    G["PepoTrainDataset.__getitem__(idx)"] --> H["get_positive_item(idx)"]
    H --> I["_positive_sample_from_row(row)"]
    I --> J["_load_pair_features(row)"]
    J --> K["_load_chain_features(chain1/2) & _process_complex"]
    I --> L["_load_pair_distance_and_mask(label_path)"]
    I --> M["crop_positive_pair(...)"]
    M --> N["distance_to_bins(...)"]
    N --> O["Return (p1_features, p2_features, label_bins, pairwise_mask, True)"]

    style G fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style H fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style J fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style M fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```
*Diagram 2: Positive sampling and feature loading pipeline execution paths.*

Sources: `[src/data/dataset.py:81-134]()`

---

## 3. Negative Sampling Pipeline

To support contrastive or non-interacting pair training, `PepoTrainDataset` provides negative sampling methods (`get_negative_item` and `get_static_negative_item`) [src/data/dataset.py:135-149](). 

Negative sampling ensures that paired chains originate from different PPI clusters (`self.items[p1_idx] != self.items[p2_idx]`) [src/data/dataset.py:136-137](). Features for both chains are processed independently and passed to `crop_negative_pair` [src/data/dataset.py:139-155](). Labels and validity masks for negative pairs are dynamically generated using `build_negative_pair_labels` based on residue positions and sequence masks, returning a binary interaction flag of `False` [src/data/dataset.py:156-167]().

Sources: `[src/data/dataset.py:135-167]()`

---

## 4. Tensor Normalization and Distance Binning

Feature processing relies heavily on tensor transformations within `_process_complex` and labeling utilities in `src/data/labels.py`. 

- **Chain Feature Files**: Chain-level `.pt` files provide precomputed residue coordinates, sequence masks, residue positions, and pre-trained language model (pLM) embeddings.
- **Tensor Normalization**: `_process_complex` standardizes shapes, applies dtype casting, and ensures mask alignment across variable-length protein chains [src/data/dataset.py:90-91]().
- **Distance Bins**: Continuous spatial distances are discretized into configurable bins defined by `distance_bin_start`, `distance_bin_end`, and `distance_bin_count` [src/data/dataset.py:32-37, 127-132]().

Sources: `[src/data/dataset.py:32-37]`, `[src/data/dataset.py:90-132]()`, `[src/data/labels.py:1-23]()`

---

# Page: Cropping, Labels and Collation

# Cropping, Labels and Collation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/collate.py](src/data/collate.py)
- [src/data/cropping.py](src/data/cropping.py)
- [src/data/labels.py](src/data/labels.py)

</details>



This page documents the spatial cropping algorithms, distance-based label engineering, and dynamic padding/collation routines used to prepare protein-protein interaction (PPI) data for training and evaluation in SurPass.

---

## 1. Spatial and Contiguous Cropping (`src/data/cropping.py`)

When protein complexes exceed memory limits or configured maximum crop sizes (default `DEFAULT_CROP_SIZE = 256`), `src/data/cropping.py` applies deterministic or stochastic cropping strategies [src/data/cropping.py:1-7].

### Key Cropping Functions

*   `select_contiguous_crop_indices(length, crop_size, start)`: Returns a contiguous slice of length `crop_size` from a sequence of length `length` [src/data/cropping.py:13-25]. If `length <= crop_size`, returns the full range [src/data/cropping.py:18-19].
*   `select_centered_contiguous_crop_indices(length, crop_size, center)`: Centers a contiguous crop around a specific residue index `center` [src/data/cropping.py:28-36].
*   `select_interface_crop_indices(contacts, n1, n2, crop_size, neighborhood_size)`: Gathers interface-centric sparse residue indices from interacting pairs using local spatial neighborhood windows (`DEFAULT_CROP_NEIGHBORHOOD_SIZE = 10`) and fills remaining slots if needed [src/data/cropping.py:97-122, src/data/cropping.py:61-94].
*   `select_contact_centered_crop_indices(contacts, n1, n2, crop_size)`: Selects a random inter-chain contact seed and builds centered contiguous crops for both interacting chains [src/data/cropping.py:125-135].
*   `crop_positive_pair(...)`: Orchestrates cropping for positive interacting pairs based on `crop_contiguous_probability` (default `0.3`) and distance thresholds (`DEFAULT_CONTACT_THRESHOLD_A = 8.0`) [src/data/cropping.py:7-11, src/data/cropping.py:166-205].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["crop_positive_pair"] --> B["inter_chain_contact_mask"]
    B --> C{ContactsExist?}
    C -- No --> D[ReturnNone]
    C -- Yes --> E{UseContiguous?}
    E -- Yes --> F["select_contact_centered_crop_indices"]
    E -- No --> G["select_interface_crop_indices"]
    F --> H["slice_complex_features"]
    G --> H
```
Sources: `src/data/cropping.py:1-205`, `src/data/labels.py:111-122`

---

## 2. Distance Binning and Label Generation (`src/data/labels.py`)

Ground truth pairwise distances are discretized into classification bins to facilitate distogram prediction objectives [src/data/labels.py:1-24].

### Distance Binning Parameters

*   `DISTANCE_BIN_START_A = 2.0` [src/data/labels.py:3]
*   `DISTANCE_BIN_END_A = 22.0` [src/data/labels.py:4]
*   `DISTANCE_BIN_WIDTH_A = 0.5` [src/data/labels.py:5]
*   `DISTANCE_BIN_NUM = 64` [src/data/labels.py:6]

### Key Label Functions

*   `distance_to_bins(distance, bin_start, bin_end, bin_count)`: Converts continuous distance tensors into discrete integer class bins via `torch.bucketize` [src/data/labels.py:11-23].
*   `inter_chain_pair_mask(p1_length, p2_length, device, total_length)`: Generates boolean masks indicating inter-chain pairs versus intra-chain pairs within a concatenated complex representation [src/data/labels.py:26-73].
*   `build_negative_pair_labels(p1_positions, p1_mask, p2_positions, p2_mask, bin_start, bin_end, bin_count)`: Computes pairwise distance matrices for non-interacting or negative protein pairs, assigning out-of-range distance bins (`bin_end + 1.0`) to unmasked residue pairs [src/data/labels.py:76-108].
*   `inter_chain_contact_mask(pairwise_dist, pairwise_mask, p1_length, contact_threshold)`: Extracts cross-chain distance sub-matrices and filters by contact threshold [src/data/labels.py:111-121].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["build_negative_pair_labels"] --> B["torch.cdist"]
    B --> C["distance_to_bins"]
    C --> D["label_bins"]
    A --> E["residue_mask"]
    E --> F["label_mask"]
```
Sources: `src/data/labels.py:1-137`

---

## 3. Batching and Collation (`src/data/collate.py`)

The collation system in `src/data/collate.py` aggregates variable-length protein-peptide pairs into uniform padded mini-batches [src/data/collate.py:1-113].

### Collation Pipeline

1.  `concat_pair_residue_features(p1, p2)`: Concatenates protein (`p1`) and peptide (`p2`) residue features along the sequence dimension. Offsets `chain_index` for the second chain (`p2_chain = p2_value.long() + p1_chain.amax() + 1`) [src/data/collate.py:24-37].
2.  `pad_first_dim(tensors)`: Pads a list of tensors along dimension 0 to match the maximum sequence length in the batch (`max_n`), using type-specific fill values (`False` for boolean, `0.0` for floats, `0` for integers) [src/data/collate.py:5-21].
3.  `collate_concatenated_pairs(proteins, peptides)`: Merges protein and peptide feature dictionaries and tracks individual chain lengths (`p1_length`, `p2_length`) [src/data/collate.py:62-72].
4.  `collate_fn(batch)`: Unpacks dataset tuples, delegates sequence collation to `collate_concatenated_pairs`, and pads 2D pair maps via `pad_pair_maps` [src/data/collate.py:75-90].
5.  `get_dataloader(...)`: Instantiates a standard PyTorch `DataLoader` with custom `collate_fn` and worker configurations [src/data/collate.py:93-112].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["collate_fn"] --> B["collate_concatenated_pairs"]
    B --> C["concat_pair_residue_features"]
    B --> D["pad_residue_dicts"]
    A --> E["pad_pair_maps"]
    D --> F["residue_batch"]
    E --> G["label_batch"]
```
Sources: `src/data/collate.py:1-113`

---

# Page: Multi-Source Balancing and Splits

# Multi-Source Balancing and Splits

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/data/__init__.py](src/data/__init__.py)
- [src/data/balancing.py](src/data/balancing.py)
- [src/train.py](src/train.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the data balancing, negative sampling, dataset splitting, and distributed weighted sampling mechanisms implemented in the `SurPass` data pipeline. These components ensure that protein-protein interaction (PPI) training data from multiple biological sources are properly partitioned, balanced with negative interacting pairs, and distributed evenly across multi-GPU environments during distributed data parallel (DDP) training.

Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:1-186]`, `[src/data/__init__.py:1-25]()`

---

## Dataset Splitting

The pipeline partitions raw dataset instances into training and testing splits deterministically using a fixed random seed. The `split_dataset` function accepts a PyTorch `Dataset` and a `test_fraction`, returning a random split of subsets [src/data/balancing.py:13-30]().

```python
def split_dataset(
    dataset: Dataset,
    test_fraction: float = 0.2,
    seed: int = 42,
) -> tuple[Dataset, Dataset]:
```

- **Validation Checks**: Verifies that `test_fraction` is strictly between `0.0` and `1.0`, and that the dataset is non-empty [src/data/balancing.py:18-21]().
- **Size Computation**: Computes test length as `max(1, int(round(len(dataset) * test_fraction)))` and guarantees a non-empty training length [src/data/balancing.py:25-28]().
- **Generator**: Uses a seeded `torch.Generator` for reproducibility across runs [src/data/balancing.py:29-30]().

Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:13-30]()`

---

## Balanced Cluster Datasets and Negative Sampling

To prevent model bias toward always predicting positive interacting interfaces, `SurPass` incorporates negative sampling via `BalancedClusterDataset` [src/data/balancing.py:33-65]() and `StaticClusterDataset` [src/data/balancing.py:108-129]().

### BalancedClusterDataset

`BalancedClusterDataset` wraps a `PepoTrainDataset` to dynamically generate negative pairs alongside positive pairs during training [src/data/balancing.py:33-40]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    BCDS["BalancedClusterDataset"] --> PTDS["PepoTrainDataset"]
    BCDS -->|Positive Index| GPI["get_positive_item(source_idx)"]
    BCDS -->|Negative Index| GNI["get_negative_item(source_idx, target_idx)"]
    
    subnl["Natural Language Space"]
    NL1["Dataset Expansion for Contrastive Learning"] --> BCDS
    NL2["Positive PPI Pair Retrieval"] --> GPI
    NL3["Non-Interacting Negative Pair Mining"] --> GNI
    
    style BCDS fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PTDS fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style GPI fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style GNI fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:33-65]`, `[src/data/balancing.py:67-91]()`

- **Length Expansion**: The dataset length is scaled by the negative ratio: `len(self.indices) * (1 + self.negative_ratio)` [src/data/balancing.py:50-51]().
- **Item Access (`__getitem__`)**:
  - Indices below `len(self.indices)` return positive items via `self.dataset.get_positive_item(source_idx)` [src/data/balancing.py:55-57]().
  - Indices beyond positive count sample a random *different* PPI cluster (`target_idx != source_idx`) to form a negative pair via `self.dataset.get_negative_item(source_idx, target_idx)` [src/data/balancing.py:59-64]().

### Helper Functions

- `_as_balanced_cluster_dataset`: Inspects the dataset type (e.g., `Subset` or `PepoTrainDataset`) and wraps it in a `BalancedClusterDataset` if `negative_ratio > 0` [src/data/balancing.py:67-91]().
- `create_balanced_split_datasets`: Combines `split_dataset` and `_as_balanced_cluster_dataset` to produce balanced train and test sets [src/data/balancing.py:94-105]().

Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:33-105]()`

---

## Distributed Weighted Sampling

When training across multiple GPUs via Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), `DistributedWeightedSampler` controls weighted sampling with replacement [src/data/balancing.py:131-182]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
    DWS["DistributedWeightedSampler"] --> WTensor["weights (1D Tensor)"]
    DWS --> Multinomial["torch.multinomial()"]
    Multinomial --> Draws["draws tensor"]
    Draws --> Slice["draws[rank :: num_replicas]"]
    
    subnl["Natural Language Space"]
    NL_DS["Epoch-level Weighted Draw"] --> DWS
    NL_DDP["Rank-Equal Sharding"] --> Slice
    
    style DWS fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style WTensor fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Multinomial fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Slice fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:131-182]()`

### Key Properties and Parameters

- **Arguments**: Takes `weights` (1D tensor of sampling weights), `num_samples`, `num_replicas`, `rank`, `seed`, and `replacement` [src/data/balancing.py:134-142]().
- **Validation**: Ensures weights are non-negative, non-empty, have a positive sum, and that `rank` lies within `[0, num_replicas)` [src/data/balancing.py:151-155]().
- **Sizing**: Rounds `total_size` up to be evenly divisible by `num_replicas` (`math.ceil(num_samples / num_replicas) * num_replicas`), yielding `num_samples_per_rank = total_size // num_replicas` [src/data/balancing.py:163-164]().

### Epoch Iteration

- `set_epoch(epoch)`: Updates the internal epoch counter used for seed offsetting [src/data/balancing.py:166-167]().
- `__iter__()`: 
  1. Instantiates a local `torch.Generator` seeded with `self.seed + self.epoch` [src/data/balancing.py:173-174]().
  2. Draws indices using `torch.multinomial(self.weights, self.total_size, replacement=self.replacement, generator=generator)` [src/data/balancing.py:175-180]().
  3. Slices the drawn indices for the current process rank: `draws[self.rank :: self.num_replicas].tolist()` [src/data/balancing.py:181]().

Sources: `[src/data/balancing.py:131-182]()`

---

# Page: Dataset Preparation Scripts

# Dataset Preparation Scripts

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py](scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py)
- [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py](scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py)
- [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py](scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py)
- [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py](scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py)
- [scripts/uniprot_sequence.py](scripts/uniprot_sequence.py)
- [scripts/uniprot_sprot.fasta.gz](scripts/uniprot_sprot.fasta.gz)

</details>



### Purpose and Scope

The `scripts/` directory houses the standalone pipelines responsible for raw data ingestion, structural feature extraction, sequence similarity filtering, protein language model (pLM) embedding generation, and external database retrieval. These scripts transform raw public databases (such as RCSB PDB, AFDB, and UniProt) into preprocessed, tensorized datasets optimized for efficient training and inference within SurPass.

---

### 1. PDB Entry Preparation Pipeline

The PDB preparation pipeline downloads structural metadata, parses sequence databases, filters out redundancies against external test sets using MMSeqs2, and identifies interacting protein-protein interfaces (PPI).

The ingestion and retrieval process is managed by `DataRetriever` [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:49-107], which downloads metadata like sequence sets, resolution indices, source maps, and SIFTS cross-references [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:57-88]. Unzipping and parsing operations are handled via helper methods such as `download_metadata()` [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:90-97] and `_read_fasta_records()` [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:135-155].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Raw PDB Metadata Sources"] -->|DataRetriever.download_metadata| B["Compressed Files in root_dir"]
    B -->|DataRetriever.unzip_metadata| C["Unzipped FASTA & TSV Index Files"]
    C -->|PDBDataSelector._read_fasta_records| D["Parsed PDB Chains"]
    D -->|MMSeqs2 Filter (30% Identity)| E["Filtered Non-Redundant Chains"]
    E -->|Atom Distance < 4.5A| F["Verified Interacting PPI Pairs"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:49-155]*

---

### 2. AFDB Domain Verification and DDI Processing

For AlphaFold Database (AFDB) domain-domain interactions (DDI), `scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py` processes local domain structures without web downloads, verifying domain integrity and computing pairwise distance labels.

Pair metadata tables are loaded and validated via `load_pair_table()` [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py:95-118], which checks for required columns (`PAIRID`, `HASH`, `CLUSTER`, `LEN`) and handles malformed entries. Domain structures are resolved from sharded directories using `resolve_domain_pdb()` [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py:157-163], and structural features are extracted via `extract_domain_features()` [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py:166-192].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Input DDI Pair Tables"] -->|load_pair_table| B["Validated DataFrame (PAIRID, HASH)"]
    B -->|resolve_domain_pdb| C["Local PDB/CIF Domain Files"]
    C -->|extract_domain_features| D["Extracted Chain Tensors (atom14, cb_positions)"]
    D -->|Distance Matrix Calculation| E["Verified Positive & Negative DDI Pairs"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py:95-192]*

---

### 3. MMSeqs2 Clustering and Similarity Filtering

Both PDB and AFDB preparation pipelines integrate MMSeqs2 to enforce strict sequence separation between training datasets and test sets. 

Sequences are clustered or searched against benchmark sets at a 30% sequence identity threshold. The pipeline groups homodimers and heterodimers separately, removing any training chains that share high similarity with evaluation benchmarks to prevent data leakage. Cluster outputs and duplicate mappings are subsequently serialized into `.tsv` files for downstream balancing scripts.

*Sources: [scripts/prepare_pdb_entries.py:1-46], [scripts/prepare_afdb_entries.py:30-41]*

---

### 4. Protein Language Model (pLM) Embedding Generation

SurPass utilizes pre-computed residue embeddings derived from the ESMC-6B model (`biohub/ESMC-6B`) [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:32]. The codebase provides two embedding generators: `scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py` for training dataset features and `scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py` for inference FASTA files.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["FASTA Records / PDB Pickles"] -->|_embed_on_devices / embed_sequences| B["load_esmc (ESMC-6B Model & Tokenizer)"]
    B -->|Forward Pass in Inference Mode| C["Hidden States Extraction"]
    C -->|Token Filtering (Remove BOS/EOS/Pad)| D["Residue Matrix [length, hidden]"]
    D -->|save_embedding / tensorize_feature_dict| E["Saved PyTorch Tensor File (.pt)"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Sources: [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:84-124], [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py:86-98]*

#### Core Embedding Functions
* `load_esmc(model_name, device)`: Instantiates `EsmcForMaskedLM` and `EsmcTokenizer` in evaluation mode [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:84-89].
* `embed_sequences(model, tokenizer, sequences)`: Tokenizes input sequences, executes model inference, strips special tokens (`BOS`, `EOS`, and padding), and returns a list of CPU float tensors of shape `[length, hidden]` [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:92-115].
* `_embed_shard(...)`: Manages multi-GPU parallelization by splitting pending records into contiguous shards assigned to distinct CUDA devices [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:165-203].

*Sources: [scripts/prepare_plm_embeddings.py:84-203], [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py:1-163]*

---

### 5. UniProt Sequence Fetching Utility

`scripts/uniprot_sequence.py` is a standalone utility that queries the UniProt REST API (`https://rest.uniprot.org`) to fetch protein records and extract amino-acid sequences [scripts/uniprot_sequence.py:17-59].

* `fetch_entry(accession, output_dir, dataset, timeout)`: Downloads JSON entries for specific UniProt accessions using `wget` [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py:21-38].
* `extract_sequence(entry)`: Parses the JSON payload to retrieve the sequence string [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py:50-59].
* `format_fasta(label, sequence, width)`: Formats sequences into standard FASTA format with configurable line width wrapping [scripts/prepare_inference_embeddings.py:71-78].

*Sources: [scripts/uniprot_sequence.py:1-79]*

---

# Page: Model Architecture

# Model Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/__init__.py](src/model/__init__.py)
- [src/model/surpass.py](src/model/surpass.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a high-level overview of the `ResOnly` network architecture [src/model/surpass.py:28-46] implemented in SurPass. The model processes protein sequences and protein Language Model (pLM) embeddings through dual concurrent streams: a 1D residue stream (`dim_token`) and a 2D pair stream (`dim_pair`). By iteratively exchanging information between token representations and pairwise distances/contacts via attention pair biases, outer product means, and triangle updates, SurPass predicts inter-chain residue contacts, residue-level binding scores, and overall protein-protein interaction (PPI) logits.

This is a parent overview page. Detailed technical implementations, tensor manipulations, and layer-by-layer mathematics are documented in the child pages linked below:
- **[ResOnly Model and SurpassOutput](#3.1)** — Forward pass orchestration, layer stacking, activation checkpointing, and prediction output heads.
- **[Embedding Layer](#3.2)** — `ResidueEmbedder`: pLM feature extraction, residue type encodings, relative position encoding (`r_max`), and initial pair construction.
- **[Transformer and Attention Primitives](#3.3)** — `ResidueTransformer`, multi-head attention with pair bias, QK LayerNorm, and attention primitives.
- **[Pair Stack: Outer Product Mean and Triangle Updates](#3.4)** — `EfficientOuterProductMean`, `TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing`, `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming`, and `PairTransition`.

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:20-46]()

---

## High-Level Architecture Overview

The SurPass architecture bridges sequence-level embeddings with 2D structural relationship maps. The network is structured around a stack of $N$ alternating blocks (`n_layers`) [src/model/surpass.py:31-88] where the residue stream and pair stream co-evolve.

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub5 ["Input Processing"]
    A["ResidueInput / pLM"] --> B["ResidueEmbedder"]
    
    subgraph Stream ["Dual-Stream Architecture"]
        B --> C["SingleRepresentation (dim_token)"]
        B --> D["PairRepresentation (dim_pair)"]
        
        C --> E["ResidueTransformer"]
        D --> F["EfficientOuterProductMean"]
        D --> G["TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing/Incoming"]
        D --> H["PairTransition"]
        
        E <-->|"Pair Bias & OPM"| F
        F --> G --> H
    end
    
    subgraph Outputs ["SurpassOutput"]
        E --> I["residue_bind_linear"]
        H --> J["pair_out_linear"]
        E --> K["protein_head"]
    end

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: High-level data flow through the `ResOnly` dual-stream architecture from `ResidueEmbedder` to `SurpassOutput` [src/model/surpass.py:143-192].*

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:143-192]()

---

## 3.1 ResOnly Model and SurpassOutput

The core orchestrator of the architecture is the `ResOnly` module [src/model/surpass.py:28-46], which manages the iterative update loops across `n_layers`. During the forward pass [src/model/surpass.py:143-192], input dictionaries are passed to the embedder, generating initial single and pair representations. Within each layer, `ResidueTransformer` updates the token stream, while `EfficientOuterProductMean`, triangle multiplication blocks, and `PairTransition` update the pair stream.

The model encapsulates its predictions in a structured `SurpassOutput` dataclass [src/model/surpass.py:20-27] containing `pair_logits`, `residue_logits`, `protein_logit`, and `pair_mask`. 

For deep technical details on the forward pass, layer sequencing, activation checkpointing (`checkpoint_pair_blocks`), and output head formulations, see **[ResOnly Model and SurpassOutput](#3.1)**.

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:20-192]()

---

## 3.2 Embedding Layer

The embedding subsystem (`ResidueEmbedder`) serves as the bridge between raw inputs (such as precomputed protein Language Model representations and sequence identities) and the internal vector spaces of `ResOnly`. It projects input features into a token dimension (`dim_token`) and initializes a 2D pairwise representation (`dim_pair`) incorporating relative position encodings governed by maximum distance parameters (`r_max`).

For detailed information on embedding combinations, feature dimensions, and relative positional encoding schemes, see **[Embedding Layer](#3.2)**.

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:68-72]()

---

## 3.3 Transformer and Attention Primitives

At the heart of the 1D feature processing stream is `ResidueTransformer` [src/model/surpass.py:76-88]. It implements multi-head attention mechanisms enhanced by 2D pair biases, allowing pairwise structural context to directly modulate residue-to-residue attention weights. It incorporates QK LayerNorm (`use_qkln`) for training stability and residue-level transition expansions.

For comprehensive architectural specifics regarding attention mechanisms, pair bias integration, and stable layer normalization, see **[Transformer and Attention Primitives](#3.3)**.

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:75-88]()

---

## 3.4 Pair Stack: Outer Product Mean and Triangle Updates

To allow 1D representations to inform 2D pairwise features, SurPass uses `EfficientOuterProductMean` [src/model/surpass.py:90-96]. Additionally, geometric constraints are propagated across the pair stream using `TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing` [src/model/surpass.py:98-103], `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming` [src/model/surpass.py:105-110], and `PairTransition` [src/model/surpass.py:112-118]. These modules ensure triangle inequality constraints and relational consistency across interacting residues.

For detailed equations, hidden dimension configurations (`dim_opm_inner`, `dim_triangle_hidden`), and tensor contraction details, see **[Pair Stack: Outer Product Mean and Triangle Updates](#3.4)**.

Sources: [src/model/surpass.py:90-118]()

---

# Page: ResOnly Model and SurpassOutput

# ResOnly Model and SurpassOutput

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/surpass.py](src/model/surpass.py)

</details>



### Purpose and Scope
This section details the primary network architecture of the codebase, centered around the `ResOnly` module and its associated output container, `SurpassOutput`. The `ResOnly` model integrates residue-level sequence embeddings with pair-level representations through an alternating stack of residue transformers and pair-updating modules (outer product mean, triangle updates, and pair transitions). It produces multi-level predictions including distograms, residue binding logits, and protein-level interaction scores.

Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:1-194]()`

---

## 1. Output Container: `SurpassOutput`

The `SurpassOutput` dataclass encapsulates the multi-scale predictions generated during the forward pass of the `ResOnly` network.

*   `pair_logits` (`torch.Tensor`): Logits representing pairwise distances or contact distributions between residues.
*   `residue_logits` (`torch.Tensor`): Logits indicating residue-level binding or interface propensity.
*   `protein_logit` (`torch.Tensor`): A global logit representing the protein-protein interaction likelihood for the complex.
*   `pair_mask` (`torch.Tensor`): Boolean mask indicating valid pairs of residues.

Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:20-27]()`

---

## 2. Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space: Architecture Mapping

The following diagram maps high-level architectural concepts to their precise classes and modules defined in the codebase.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Protein Sequence & pLM Inputs"] --> B["ResidueEmbedder src/model/components/embedder.py"]
    B --> C["Residue Stream single_repr"]
    B --> D["Pair Stream pair_repr"]
    
    C --> E["ResidueTransformer src/model/components/transformer.py"]
    D --> F["EfficientOuterProductMean src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py"]
    D --> G["TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing src/model/components/triangle_update.py"]
    D --> H["TriangleMultiplicationIncoming src/model/components/triangle_update.py"]
    D --> I["PairTransition src/model/components/primitives.py"]
    
    E --> J["Output Heads pair_out_linear, residue_bind_linear, protein_head"]
    D --> J
    J --> K["SurpassOutput src/model/surpass.py"]

    subgraph "Natural Language Concepts"
        L1["Residue Embedding"]
        L2["Residue Transformer Stack"]
        L3["Pair Stack Updates"]
        L4["Multi-Scale Output Container"]
    end
```
Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:8-15]`, `[src/model/surpass.py:20-27]`, `[src/model/surpass.py:68-129]()`

---

## 3. Model Initialization and Hyperparameters

The `ResOnly` class initializes dimensions, attention heads, and module lists for the multi-layer network.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Init["ResOnly.__init__"] --> Check["Dimension & Head Validation"]
    Check --> Embedder["ResidueEmbedder"]
    Check --> Layers["Iterative Stack Construction n_layers"]
    
    Layers --> RT["ResidueTransformer"]
    Layers --> EOPM["EfficientOuterProductMean"]
    Layers --> TO["TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing"]
    Layers --> TI["TriangleMultiplicationIncoming"]
    Layers --> PT["PairTransition"]
    
    Init --> Heads["Output Heads LayerNorm & Linear"]
    Heads --> S1["pair_out_linear"]
    Heads --> S2["residue_bind_linear"]
    Heads --> S3["protein_head"]
```
Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:28-132]()`

### Parameter Validation & Configuration
During `__init__`, `ResOnly` enforces several structural rules:
*   `dim_token` must be cleanly divisible by `n_heads` (`[src/model/surpass.py:48-51]()`).
*   `num_classes` must match `xt_pair_dist_dim` (`[src/model/surpass.py:52-58]()`).
*   `contact_bins` must be within the range `1..num_classes` (`[src/model/surpass.py:59-62]()`).

Component modules are instantiated across `n_layers`:
*   `self.residue_blocks`: A `nn.ModuleList` of `ResidueTransformer` instances (`[src/model/surpass.py:75-88]()`).
*   `self.outer_product_mean`: A `nn.ModuleList` of `EfficientOuterProductMean` instances (`[src/model/surpass.py:90-96]()`).
*   `self.triangle_multiplication_outgoing`: A `nn.ModuleList` of `TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing` instances (`[src/model/surpass.py:98-104]()`).
*   `self.triangle_multiplication_incoming`: A `nn.ModuleList` of `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming` instances (`[src/model/surpass.py:105-111]()`).
*   `self.pair_blocks`: A `nn.ModuleList` of `PairTransition` instances (`[src/model/surpass.py:112-118]()`).

Parameters for OPM and pair transition linear layers are zero-initialized via `reset_parameters()` (`[src/model/surpass.py:133-142]()`).

Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:28-142]()`

---

## 4. Forward Pass Execution Flow

The forward pass processes a residue batch dictionary, executes the alternating residue-pair block stack, and computes final outputs.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["residue_batch Dict"] --> Extract["Filter Length Keys & ResidueEmbedder"]
    Extract --> Embed["single_repr, pair_repr, mask"]
    Embed --> LoopInit["For i in range n_layers"]
    
    LoopInit --> Trans["single_repr = ResidueTransformer"]
    Trans --> PairStack["pair_repr = _apply_pair_stack i"]
    
    PairStack --> CheckMore{"i < n_layers - 1?"}
    CheckMore -- Yes --> LoopInit
    CheckMore -- No --> Heads["Compute Output Projections"]
    
    Heads --> PairLog["pair_logits Symmetrization & Contact Bias"]
    Heads --> ResLog["residue_logits Residue Bind Head"]
    Heads --> ProtLog["protein_logit Protein Head"]
    
    PairLog --> Output["SurpassOutput Container"]
    ResLog --> Output
    ProtLog --> Output
```
Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:143-192]()`

### Step-by-Step Data Flow
1.  **Embedding Extraction**: Length keys (`p1_length`, `p2_length`) are filtered out of the residue batch before passing inputs to `residue_embedder` (`[src/model/surpass.py:147-152]()`).
2.  **Mask Generation**: The returned mask is converted to a boolean tensor, and a pairwise mask (`pair_mask`) is derived via outer boolean conjunction (`[src/model/surpass.py:153-155]()`).
3.  **Iterative Layer Stack**: For each layer up to `n_layers`:
    *   `single_repr` is updated through `ResidueTransformer` (`[src/model/surpass.py:158-163]()`).
    *   `pair_repr` is updated through the pair stack via `_apply_pair_stack` (`[src/model/surpass.py:164-170]()`).
4.  **Pair Logits Projection**: Pair representations are normalized using `pair_out_layernorm`, projected via `pair_out_linear`, symmetrized, and adjusted with contact bin biases (`[src/model/surpass.py:172-180]()`).
5.  **Residue Logits Projection**: Single representations are normalized via `residue_bind_norm` and projected through `residue_bind_linear` to produce residue-level logits, masked out for invalid positions (`[src/model/surpass.py:175-178]()`).
6.  **Protein Logit Computation**: Global protein-level interaction scores are computed by `_protein_logit` using concatenated representations and sequence lengths (`[src/model/surpass.py:181-186]()`).

Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:143-192]()`

---

## 5. Output Heads and Post-Processing

*   **Pair Symmetrization**: Raw pair logits are symmetrized by averaging with their transposed counterpart:
    $$\text{logits} = \frac{\text{logits} + \text{logits}^T}{2}$$
    `[src/model/surpass.py:173-174]()`
*   **Protein Head**: Implemented as a sequential network consisting of a `LayerNorm` (operating on `dim_token * 3`), a `Linear` projection to `dim_token`, a `GELU` activation, and a final `Linear` projection to `1` (`[src/model/surpass.py:124-129]()`).

Sources: `[src/model/surpass.py:124-129]`, `[src/model/surpass.py:172-192]()`

---

# Page: Embedding Layer

# Embedding Layer

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/components/embedder.py](src/model/components/embedder.py)
- [src/model/components/rotary.py](src/model/components/rotary.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
The embedding layer constructs initial representations for residues and residue pairs in the SurPass architecture. It processes protein language model (pLM) embeddings, categorical residue types, absolute indices, chain identifiers, and biophysical energy calculations (via CALVADOS) to produce rich starting tensors for downstream transformer and pair-stack modules.

Sources: `src/model/components/embedder.py:1-203`

---

## Positional and Index Embeddings

Positional information is integrated via sine/cosine index embeddings and relative position encodings that account for chain boundaries and sequence separations up to a maximum distance parameter `r_max`.

### Absolute Index Embeddings
The function `get_index_embedding` computes standard sinusoidal positional encodings for a given set of integer indices:
- Takes `indices` of shape `[n]` or `[b, n]`.
- Computes sinusoidal frequencies across dimension `edim`.
- Returns positional embeddings of shape `[n, edim]` or `[b, n, edim]`.

```python
def get_index_embedding(indices, edim, max_len=2056):
    ...
```
*Implementation reference:* `src/model/components/embedder.py:120-149`

### Relative Position Encoding
The function `relative_position_encoding` constructs pairwise relative representations combining token distance, residue index offsets, and chain identity flags:
- `same_chain_mask`: Binary indicator of whether two residues belong to the same chain (`src/model/components/embedder.py:162`).
- `d_residue`: Clipped residue index difference bounded by `r_max` (`src/model/components/embedder.py:166-169`).
- `d_token`: Global position encoding offset (`src/model/components/embedder.py:175-178`).
- Outputs a concatenated one-hot feature tensor `rel_pos` of shape `[b, n, n, 2 + 4 * (r_max + 1)]` masked by valid pair masks (`src/model/components/embedder.py:183-184`).

Sources: `src/model/components/embedder.py:120-185`

---

## Biophysical Potential Integration (CALVADOS)

To incorporate physical priors into pairwise representations, the embedding module computes residue-residue interaction energies using the CALVADOS model (Ashbaugh-Hatch hydrophobic interactions and Yukawa electrostatic potentials).

- `normalize_calvados_energy`: Applies $\text{arcsinh}(E/kT)$ compression to maintain linear behavior in attractive wells while compressing Lennard-Jones walls (`src/model/components/embedder.py:30-32`).
- `build_calvados_bin_energy_table`: Generates a cached `[20, 20, dim]` tensor of pairwise energy values mapped across distance bins (`src/model/components/embedder.py:94-116`).
- `_cached_calvados_bin_energy_table`: Uses `lru_cache` to avoid redundant physics re-computations (`src/model/components/embedder.py:84-91`).

Sources: `src/model/components/embedder.py:30-117`

---

## Pairwise Distance Binning

Pairwise Euclidean distances computed from residue coordinates are discretized into one-hot histograms using linear binning limits:
- `bin_pairwise_distances`: Calculates pairwise distance matrices of shape `[b, n, n]` from coordinate tensors `[b, n, 3]` and maps them to one-hot bin representations (`src/model/components/embedder.py:187-203`).

Sources: `src/model/components/embedder.py:187-203`

---

# Page: Transformer and Attention Primitives

# Transformer and Attention Primitives

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py](src/model/components/calvados_functions.py)
- [src/model/components/calvados_residues.pickle](src/model/components/calvados_residues.pickle)
- [src/model/components/primitives.py](src/model/components/primitives.py)
- [src/model/components/transformer.py](src/model/components/transformer.py)
- [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py](src/model/components/triangle_attention.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page details the foundational building blocks, attention mechanisms, update primitives, and physical energy functions residing in `src/model/components/`. These primitives form the structural backbone of SurPass's residue and pair streams, enabling residue-level feature updates, pair-conditioned multi-head attention, geometric triangle attention, and integration with the CALVADOS coarse-grained force field.

---

## 1. Primitive Modules and Activation Functions

SurPass implements custom neural network primitives tailored for structural biology models, featuring adaptive normalizations, gated activation functions, and transition blocks.

### Adaptive Layer Normalization (`AdaptiveLayerNorm` and `AdaptiveLayerNormOutputScale`)
`AdaptiveLayerNorm` applies a standard LayerNorm with element-wise affine parameters ($\gamma$ and $\beta$) dynamically generated from conditioning variables (e.g., global or context embeddings) via linear projections and a sigmoid activation on $\gamma$ [src/model/components/primitives.py:11-43](). `AdaptiveLayerNormOutputScale` applies zero-initialized gating to scale representations conditioned on auxiliary signals [src/model/components/primitives.py:45-73]().

### Gated Linear Units and Transitions (`SwiGLU`, `Transition`, `PairTransition`)
* **`SwiGLU`**: Splits the input tensor along the final dimension into two halves, applying the SiLU (Swish) activation function to the gate half before element-wise multiplication [src/model/components/primitives.py:75-88]().
* **`Transition` / `PairTransition`**: Feed-forward blocks that expand hidden dimensions by an `expansion_factor` (default 4), apply `SwiGLU`, and project back to the model dimension, with an optional initial LayerNorm [src/model/components/primitives.py:90-151]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Code Entity Space"]
        IN["Input Tensor (x)"] --> LN["torch.nn.LayerNorm"]
        LN --> SWI["SwiGLU (src/model/components/primitives.py:75)"]
        SWI --> LIN["Linear Out (src/model/components/primitives.py:106)"]
        LIN --> MASK["Mask Multiplication"]
    end
    
    style IN fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style LN fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style SWI fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style LIN fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style MASK fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Sources: `[src/model/components/primitives.py:11-151]()`*

---

## 2. Attention Mechanisms and QK LayerNorm

Multi-head attention in SurPass incorporates query-key layer normalization (`qk_layernorm`), rotary position embeddings (`RotaryEmbedding`), and pair-wise bias terms.

### `GatedAttention`
`GatedAttention` computes standard self-attention over residue sequences with integrated rotary position embeddings and an output gating mechanism [src/model/components/transformer.py:40-138](). 

* **QKV Projection**: Projects input features `d_model` into queries, keys, and values of inner dimension `n_heads * d_head` [src/model/components/transformer.py:59]() alongside a gate projection `g_proj` [src/model/components/transformer.py:61]().
* **QK LayerNorm**: Applies `nn.LayerNorm` independently to queries and keys prior to rotary embedding application to stabilize attention logits [src/model/components/transformer.py:64-70]().
* **Rotary Embedding**: Applies `RotaryEmbedding` to the unflattened head dimensions of $Q$ and $K$ [src/model/components/transformer.py:71-80]().
* **Scaled Dot-Product Attention**: Leverages `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention` (SDPA) with key padding masks [src/model/components/transformer.py:114-121]().
* **Output Gating**: Multiplies attention outputs by the sigmoid of the gate projection `g` before the final linear projection [src/model/components/transformer.py:135]().

### `PairBiasAttention`
`PairBiasAttention` integrates pair-wise representations (`pair_feats`) directly into the attention score matrix as additive bias terms [src/model/components/transformer.py:141-194]().

* **Pair Bias Projection**: When `pair_dim` is provided, pair features are normalized and projected via `nn.Linear(pair_dim, heads, bias=False)` to yield per-head spatial biases [src/model/components/transformer.py:171-175]().
* **Logit Modification**: The projected pair bias is added directly to the $QK^T$ attention matrix before softmax normalization.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["Attention Architecture & Code Entities"]
        InputNode["node_feats (b,n,d_s)"] --> QKV["to_qkv (Transformer.py:165)"]
        InputPair["pair_feats (b,n,n,d_e)"] --> PairNorm["pair_norm (Transformer.py:173)"]
        PairNorm --> ToBias["to_bias (Transformer.py:172)"]
        QKV --> QKLN["q_layer_norm / k_layer_norm (Transformer.py:169)"]
        QKLN --> QKMatMul["Scaled Dot Product + Pair Bias"]
        ToBias --> QKMatMul
        QKMatMul --> Gate["to_g Output Gate (Transformer.py:166)"]
        Gate --> OutNode["to_out_node (Transformer.py:167)"]
    end

    style InputNode fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style InputPair fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style QKV fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PairNorm fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style ToBias fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style QKLN fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style QKMatMul fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Gate fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style OutNode fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Sources: `[src/model/components/transformer.py:40-194]()`*

---

## 3. Triangle Attention Primitives

To update pair representations along geometric triangle inequalities (AlphaFold2/OpenFold style), SurPass implements specialized triangle attention modules.

### `BiasGatedAttention`
`BiasGatedAttention` executes multi-head attention on pair tensors `[*, I, J, C]` using multiple additive bias tensors (e.g., masking and triangle bias) and an output gating projection [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:12-56]().

### `TriangleAttention` (`TriangleAttentionStartingNode` & `TriangleAttentionEndingNode`)
`TriangleAttention` operates on pair representations `[*, I, J, C_in]` by treating either starting nodes or ending nodes as the sequence dimension [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:58-164]().

* **Orientation**: 
  * `TriangleAttentionStartingNode` sets `starting=True` (Algorithm 13 equivalent) [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:151-156]().
  * `TriangleAttentionEndingNode` sets `starting=False` (Algorithm 14 equivalent), transposing dimensions `-2` and `-3` prior to processing [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:159-164]().
* **Triangle Bias**: Computes a linear projection of LayerNorm-normalized pair features, permutes dimensions, and adds it as an attention bias alongside sequence masks [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:138-139]().
* **Chunking**: Supports optional sequence chunking (`_chunk`) to reduce memory consumption during large-scale pair updates [src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:96-115]().

*Sources: `[src/model/components/triangle_attention.py:1-164]()`*

---

## 4. CALVADOS Force Field and Energy Functions

SurPass includes support for the CALVADOS coarse-grained polymer physics model (`calvados_functions.py`), enabling physical energy calculations based on residue-specific interaction parameters [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:1-121]().

### `CalvadosModel` Dataclass
Encapsulates physical interaction maps and parameters [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:9-19]():
* `sigmamap`: DataFrame of pairwise Lennard-Jones distance parameters $\sigma_{ij}$ [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:11]().
* `lambdamap`: DataFrame of hydrophobicity scaling parameters $\lambda_{ij}$ [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:12]().
* `yukawa_eps`: DataFrame of electrostatic coupling amplitudes [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:13]().
* `yukawa_kappa`: Debye-Huckel screening parameter derived from salt concentration [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:14]().

### Key Functions
* `load_calvados_model`: Loads residue pickle tables (`calvados_residues.pickle`), adjusts histidine charge states based on pH, computes Bjerrum length, and constructs pairwise parameter matrices [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:34-80]().
* `compute_ashbaugh_hatch`: Calculates the Ashbaugh-Hatch functional form for hydrophobicity-scaled Lennard-Jones interactions with switching functions [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:100-110]().
* `compute_yukawa`: Computes screened electrostatic interactions via Yukawa potential [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:112-116]().
* `compute_calvados_energy`: Combines Ashbaugh-Hatch and Yukawa terms to yield total coarse-grained interaction energies [src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:118-121]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode["CALVADOS Physics Integration"]
        Pickle["calvados_residues.pickle"] --> Load["load_calvados_model (calvados_functions.py:34)"]
        Load --> Model["CalvadosModel Dataclass (calvados_functions.py:9)"]
        Model --> AH["compute_ashbaugh_hatch (calvados_functions.py:100)"]
        Model --> YU["compute_yukawa (calvados_functions.py:112)"]
        AH --> Energy["compute_calvados_energy (calvados_functions.py:118)"]
        YU --> Energy
    end

    style Pickle fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Load fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Model fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style AH fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style YU fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style Energy fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Sources: `[src/model/components/calvados_functions.py:1-121](), [src/model/components/calvados_residues.pickle:1-8]()`*

# Page: Pair Stack: Outer Product Mean and Triangle Updates

# Pair Stack: Outer Product Mean and Triangle Updates

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py](src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py)
- [src/model/components/triangle_update.py](src/model/components/triangle_update.py)
- [src/model/optimizer.py](src/model/optimizer.py)
- [src/utils/model_utils.py](src/utils/model_utils.py)
- [src/utils/nan_monitor.py](src/utils/nan_monitor.py)

</details>



This section details the components responsible for updating the pair representation tensor ($Z$) within the SurPass architecture. Specifically, it covers the memory-efficient outer product mean (`EfficientOuterProductMean`), triangle multiplicative updates for outgoing and incoming paths (`TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing` and `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming`), numerical stabilization via `_stable_triangle_matmul`, and their coordination within the model's pair stack.

---

## 1. Efficient Outer Product Mean (`EfficientOuterProductMean`)

The outer product mean translates token-level (residue stream) representations into pair-level updates without materializing the massive intermediate $[N_{res}, N_{res}, C_{hidden}, C_{hidden}]$ tensor required by traditional implementations. 

`EfficientOuterProductMean` normalizes the input token representation, projects it to a hidden channel dimension without bias, and computes the outer product using batched Einstein summation (`torch.einsum`) [src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py:25-47]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["InputTokenRepr"] --> B["nn.LayerNorm"]
    B --> C["LinearNoBias"]
    C --> D["Masking"]
    D --> E["ProjectedEinsum"]
    E --> F["OuterProductEinsum"]
    F --> G["OutputPairTensor"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Diagram 1: Data flow in `EfficientOuterProductMean` mapping conceptual steps to tensor operations.*

Sources: `src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py:25-47`

---

## 2. Triangle Multiplicative Updates

Triangle updates propagate structural information across graph edges (pairs) by enforcing triangular inequalities. SurPass implements both outgoing and incoming variants derived from AlphaFold architectures [src/model/components/triangle_update.py:24-121]().

### Base Class: `TriangleMultiplicativeUpdate`
The base module performs LayerNorm on the input pair tensor $z$, computes two separate linear projections $a$ and $b$ modulated by gating sigmoid networks, combines them, applies another LayerNorm and output projection, and gates the final residual output [src/model/components/triangle_update.py:24-90]().

### Outgoing Update (`TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing`)
Implements the outgoing triangle multiplicative update by overriding `_combine_projections` using `_stable_triangle_matmul` on permuted final dimensions [src/model/components/triangle_update.py:92-106]().

### Incoming Update (`TriangleMultiplicationIncoming`)
Implements the incoming triangle multiplicative update by modifying the transposition permutation order prior to contractive multiplication [src/model/components/triangle_update.py:108-121]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    H["PairInputZ"] --> I["LayerNormIn"]
    I --> J["ProjectionsAandB"]
    J --> K["CombineProjections"]
    K --> L["StableTriangleMatmul"]
    L --> M["LayerNormOut"]
    M --> N["GatedOutputZ"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Diagram 2: Processing pipeline for `TriangleMultiplicativeUpdate` subclasses.*

Sources: `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:24-122`

---

## 3. Stable Triangle Matrix Multiplication

To prevent numerical overflow or `Inf` propagation through LayerNorm layers during matrix contraction over the hidden dimension $K$, `_stable_triangle_matmul` executes the contraction in single-precision (`fp32`) and scales the output by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$ [src/model/components/triangle_update.py:15-22]().

```python
def _stable_triangle_matmul(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    k = int(a.shape[-1])
    out = torch.matmul(a.float(), b.float())
    if k > 0:
        out = out * (float(k) ** -0.5)
    return out
```

Sources: `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:15-22`

---

## 4. Code Entity Mapping & Integration

The following mapping associates the natural language concepts of pair stack operations with their concrete classes and helper functions in the codebase.

| Conceptual Operation / Component | Code Entity (Class / Function) | File Path |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Memory-Efficient OPM | `EfficientOuterProductMean` | `src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py:25` |
| Standard Chunked OPM | `OuterProductMean` | `src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py:49` |
| Stable Triangle Matmul | `_stable_triangle_matmul` | `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:15` |
| Triangle Outgoing Update | `TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing` | `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:92` |
| Triangle Incoming Update | `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming` | `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:108` |
| Tensor Dimension Permutation | `permute_final_dims` | `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:9` |

Sources: `src/model/components/outer_product_mean.py:25-75`, `src/model/components/triangle_update.py:9-122`
